title: What drinking seawater does to your body 🌊
subject: ocean
description:
Would you take one sip if you were stranded? 👇

Why can't you drink seawater? Your kidneys can't make urine salty enough to get rid of it, so every sip dehydrates you further.

Sources: NOAA Ocean Service (Can humans drink seawater?), Live Science (Why can't we drink saltwater?, with Rob DeSalle, American Museum of Natural History)
tags: what happens if you drink salt water

scenes.text: You can die of thirst floating in the ocean.
Seawater is about 3.5 percent salt by weight. That's more than 3 times saltier than your blood.
Your kidneys can't match it. According to NOAA, they can only make urine that's less salty than seawater.
So to flush out the salt, you'd have to pee more water than you drank. Every sip leaves you thirstier.
Rob DeSalle of the American Museum of Natural History puts it plainly: saltwater can never quench your thirst.
